SECTION D: Long Answer Type Questions (5 Marks Each)

Q30. (a) Explain the process of unification of Germany.  
OR  
(b) Explain the process of unification of Italy.

Answer / Solution:
(a) Explain the process of unification of Germany. 
Middle-class movement: In 1848, middle-class Germans tried to unite the region 
but were repressed by the monarchy. 
Prussia’s Role: Prussia took leadership under Chief Minister Otto von Bismarck. 
Process: Bismarck used the “Blood and Iron” policy. Three wars over seven years 
(vs Austria, Denmark, France) ended in Prussian victory. 
Result: In 1871, the Prussian King, William I, was proclaimed German Emperor at 
Versailles. 

OR (b) Explain the process of unification of Italy. 
Fragmentation: Italy was divided into seven states; only Sardinia-Piedmont was 
ruled by an Italian. 
Mazzini: Formed ‘Young Italy’ for a unitary republic. 
Cavour: The Chief Minister of Sardinia-Piedmont led the movement diplomatically, 
defeating Austrian forces in 1859. 
Garibaldi: Marched into South Italy (1860) with “Red Shirts” and won peasant 
support to drive out Spanish rulers. 
Result: In 1861, Victor Emmanuel II was proclaimed King of United Italy.
